intro.data: One lifted line must run TWO crates: a starter crate and a heavier crate. Lift a three-step pipeline — Restock (+1), Double (x2), Seal (+5) — across the batch world, either stepwise (Batch Restocker, Batch Doubler, Batch Sealer) or with pre-lifted composites. The tray hides a sly 'Reset-to-4' lift that matches the Batch Restocker on the starter crate but stalls every item to 4 on the heavier one. A line that only ships the starter crate right is still wrong; build the lift that nails BOTH.
intro.alchemy: One lifted process must refine TWO crates: a starter crate and a heavier crate. Lift a three-step process — Restock (+1), Double (x2), Seal (+5) — across the crate world, either stepwise (Crate Restocker, Crate Doubler, Crate Sealer) or with pre-lifted composites. The tray hides a sly 'Reset-to-4' apparatus that matches the Crate Restocker on the starter crate but stalls every item to 4 on the heavier one. A process that only refines the starter crate is still false; build the lift that nails BOTH.
intro.spellcraft: One lifted rite must bind TWO flocks: a starter flock and a heavier flock. Lift a three-step rite — Restock (+1), Double (x2), Seal (+5) — across the flock world, either stepwise (Flock Restocker, Flock Doubler, Flock Sealer) or with pre-lifted composites. The tray hides a sly 'Reset-to-4' working that matches the Flock Restocker on the starter flock but stalls every item to 4 on the heavier one. A rite that only binds the starter flock is still hollow; build the lift that nails BOTH.
intro.abstract: F(x) means the value x lifted into the batch world (the box holding x), and a lift F(f) does f to each item inside, so F(g∘f) = F(g)∘F(f). One lifted line F(A)→F(B)→F(C)→F(D) must satisfy two cases over the same F(A) and F(D): case 1 sends F(3) ↦ F(13), case 2 sends F(4) ↦ F(15). Lift f (+1), g (×2), h (+5) stepwise or as pre-lifted composites; the impostor F(f)? (set every item to 4) coincides with F(f) on F(3) but diverges on F(4), so it passes case 1 and fails case 2. Build the one lift that passes both and leave the impostors in the tray.

afterSuccess.data: One lifted line shipped both crates: Batch Restocker, Batch Doubler, Batch Sealer sent F(3) to F(13) and F(4) to F(15). The 'Reset-to-4' lift matched the Restocker on the starter crate by coincidence but stalled the heavier one, passing the easy case and failing the hard one. The second crate is why lifting must be the genuine lift of each step, not a step that merely agrees once: F(h∘g∘f) = F(h)∘F(g)∘F(f).
afterSuccess.alchemy: One lifted process refined both crates: Crate Restocker, Crate Doubler, Crate Sealer sent F(3) to F(13) and F(4) to F(15). 'Reset-to-4' matched the Restocker on the starter crate by coincidence but stalled the heavier one, passing the easy case and failing the hard one. The second crate is why lifting must be the genuine lift of each step: F(h∘g∘f) = F(h)∘F(g)∘F(f).
afterSuccess.spellcraft: One lifted rite bound both flocks: Flock Restocker, Flock Doubler, Flock Sealer sent F(3) to F(13) and F(4) to F(15). 'Reset-to-4' matched the Restocker on the starter flock by coincidence but stalled the heavier one, passing the easy case and failing the hard one. The second flock is why lifting must be the genuine lift of each step: F(h∘g∘f) = F(h)∘F(g)∘F(f).
afterSuccess.abstract: The faithful lifted line F(h)∘F(g)∘F(f) sent F(3) ↦ F(13) and F(4) ↦ F(15). F(f)? (set-to-4) coincides with F(f) at F(3) (both give F(4)), so it passes case 1, but at F(4) it gives F(4) not F(5) and fails case 2. Two cases pin the lift: agreeing on one box is not the same lift — and by functoriality F(h∘g∘f) = F(h)∘F(g)∘F(f).

reveal.summary: A functor preserves composition, so lifting a whole pipeline equals composing the lifts: F(h ∘ g ∘ f) = F(h) ∘ F(g) ∘ F(f). Two test cases over one lifted line force every lifted step to be the genuine lift, not coincidentally right on a single box; an impostor lift that matches a faithful step on one box still corrupts the line on another.
notation: F(h ∘ g ∘ f) = F(h) ∘ F(g) ∘ F(f) : F(A) → F(D)
reveal.moreFormal: F applied to a value carries it into the target category; F applied to a morphism carries the arrow. Functoriality (F(g∘f)=F(g)∘F(f), F(id)=id) means a chain of lifts equals the lift of the chain.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: map(h ∘ g ∘ f) === map(h) ∘ map(g) ∘ map(f); a single test input can pass an impostor stage — a second input catches it.
